aoi.name: Forli bounded pilot
aoi.selectionBasis: Bounded engineering pilot around Forli and the Montone-Rabbi system. Declared IMERG, CLC, Copernicus DEM, XDBTR and regional event-2 coverage all contain this bbox; the common evaluation grid retains an explicit cell-centre AOI mask.

routingBaselines.methodologyNote: Unconditioned D8 steepest-positive-gradient routing over GLO-30, with AOI-edge, known-water and local-depression terminals. Known DBTR permanent-water presence is incomplete. This baseline is terrain flow concentration, not inundation extent, water depth, flood probability or an operational forecast.

Complete real IMERG V07 Final Run 48-hour accumulation is nearest-sampled from its native 0.1 degree grid onto the frozen 30 m representation. Canonical CLC/slope runoff is converted to local volume and propagated without loss over the frozen unconditioned D8 graph. The current DBTR known-water mask remains historically incomplete. This is event runoff flow concentration, not inundation extent, water depth, flood probability or an operational forecast.

evaluationProtocols.methodologyNote: Frozen before reading the official event-2 geometry. The score is routed upstream excess volume on the finite frozen AOI grid. ROC AUC and average precision are threshold-free ranking diagnostics; overlap is reported only at predeclared area fractions with fractional tie weighting. These diagnostics evaluate spatial concentration against observed inundation labels but do not convert concentration into predicted inundation extent, validate water depth or calibrate a threshold.

evaluationRuns.methodologyNote: The V7 geometry was first loaded only after protocol commit 110a217 was published. Independent scikit-learn verification reproduces the ROC AUC and average precision. The near-random result is retained as negative evidence that unconditioned D8 runoff concentration does not reconstruct the observed event-2 flood extent; no threshold was calibrated and no inundation, water-depth or forecast claim is made.

observationComparisonProtocols.methodologyNote: Frozen from the public Dext3r station/variable catalogue before requesting or reading the Dext3r event series. The annual validated PDFs had already been inspected to establish their daily resolution, station coverage and event context, so this is not claimed as blind with respect to every ARPAE value. Rainfall stations are selected by inclusion in the frozen pilot and gauge semantics; hydrometric stations follow the Montone river axis plus the Rabbi tributary. Their local datums are not arithmetically comparable. Dext3r observations remain post-event comparison evidence, are never calibration inputs, and missing or incomplete records never become zero. The V7 inundation extent is not used in station selection or this comparison.

observationComparisonRuns.methodologyNote: Materialized after the comparison protocol freeze from Dext3r request be86675d-a290-4208-8b38-0bb420396ca0. Hourly rain is summed over the exact half-open 48-hour window and compared with the nearest native 0.1 degree IMERG cell. Empty Dext3r value fields remain missing; numeric zero is preserved. Hydrometric values remain relative to each station's local datum and are used only for within-station timing and change. This run does not calibrate the routing model and is not an inundation or hydraulic validation.

requiredBoundaryEvidence.acceptanceCriteria: The existing content-addressed 48-hour IMERG, CLC and GLO-30 receipts reproduce deterministic local runoff without missing required cells.
A pre-event forcing window and an explicit, versioned initial-wetness or model-warmup transformation cover the antecedent May rainfall without using the observed inundation extent.
requiredBoundaryEvidence.blocker: The current forcing begins at 2023-05-16T00:00:00Z and does not represent the wet initial state left by the earlier May event.

requiredBoundaryEvidence.acceptanceCriteria: Time-varying Montone and Rabbi inflows cover the full event window as discharge, or as stage paired with station datum, cross-section and a high-flow-calibrated event-valid rating relation; the valid range, calibration/validation events, non-bijective or flood-loop behaviour, uncertainty and gaps remain explicit.
requiredBoundaryEvidence.blocker: Dext3r supplies local-datum stage, its public daily-discharge catalogue ends before the May 2023 event for the target stations, and the Rabbi/Predappio stage series is incomplete. The regional Commission report states that its hourly Montone/Castrocaro reconstruction used an ARPAE 2022 rating curve and publishes a plotted hydrograph plus volume balance, but it provides neither the machine-readable discharge series nor the rating-curve formula/table and supplies no Rabbi discharge hydrograph. ARPAE DET-2024-723 states that the available Castrocaro relation was calibrated only on direct low-flow measurements and separately commissioned high-flow calibration; neither the resulting numerical relation nor the Montone-Rabbi calibration hydrographs are public in the audited sources.

requiredBoundaryEvidence.acceptanceCriteria: A full-window downstream stage in a declared vertical datum, a discharge boundary, or a documented rating relation is pinned at or beyond the hydraulic domain outlet.
requiredBoundaryEvidence.blocker: Ponte Braldo and Ponte Vico stage series are complete but remain relative to separate local station datums and cannot be converted into a hydraulic boundary without datum and rating information.

requiredBoundaryEvidence.acceptanceCriteria: Each breach used by the replay has source-backed coordinates, bank side, activation time, crest/invert elevation and a width/evolution model with uncertainty; the flood extent is not used to infer these values.
requiredBoundaryEvidence.blocker: The official repair account and 2024 special-plan monograph identify named breach/overtopping locations and only partial bank-side context; neither provides machine-readable coordinates, activation times, elevations, width evolution or breach hydrographs.

requiredBoundaryEvidence.acceptanceCriteria: Pre-event embankment alignment and crest elevations cover the hydraulic domain with declared survey/reference dates and vertical datum; post-event repairs are excluded or separately represented.
requiredBoundaryEvidence.blocker: The DBTR extract is a post-event known-presence window and the official event sources describe failures/repairs without crest elevations. The bounded PST representation retains source no-data on critical embankment cells and does not supply a complete historical crest surface.

requiredBoundaryEvidence.acceptanceCriteria: A bounded pre-event bare-earth terrain surface covers the domain, retains horizontal/vertical CRS, source epoch, resolution, nodata and transformation provenance, and represents critical embankments without silent interpolation.
requiredBoundaryEvidence.blocker: The pinned 5 m nearest-neighbour PST representation preserves 11.064985% source no-data, including gaps on riverbed, embankment and permanent-water center cells, so it cannot serve as the sole hydraulic terrain source. The available GLO-30 input is a 30 m DSM rather than hydraulic-grade bare-earth terrain.

requiredBoundaryEvidence.acceptanceCriteria: The Montone and Rabbi channel representation declares bed/cross-section geometry, structures and roughness parameters with source and model versions for the bounded domain.
requiredBoundaryEvidence.blocker: DBTR supplies planimetric riverbed geometry only. The official PAI relation states that a steady-flow HEC-RAS model and calibrated roughness existed, but the three pinned public archives contain only 19 DWG drawings and no HEC-RAS projects, numeric cross-sections, event-valid roughness or 2023 boundary conditions.

conditionedReplayProtocols.methodologyNote: This protocol is frozen after the V7 extent and ARPAE comparison values were already loaded for earlier diagnostics, so it is explicitly post-hoc and not a blind hindcast. It freezes the conditioned-input gate before acquiring new rating curves, discharge hydrographs, breach parameters, crest elevations or channel parameters. Passing the gate would authorize only a diagnostic conditioned replay with separately versioned inputs and parameters; it would not constitute independent validation. A future validation claim requires a new event or spatial holdout whose reference remains withheld until prediction freeze.

conditionedReplaySourceAudits.methodologyNote: Materialized from the official 2023 ARPAE Annale after the conditioned-input protocol was frozen. Page 17 defines stage relative to the gauge zero and the guillemet symbol as missing data. Page 26 publishes gauge-zero elevations for Castrocaro, Predappio and Ponte Vico while Ponte Braldo is explicitly missing. Pages 54 and 65 retain daily stage observations, gaps and maximum-increment context. Pages 68-69 define discharge semantics and list 45 discharge-measurement stations, but neither Montone nor Rabbi appears. The Annale therefore does not supply an event-valid rating curve or discharge hydrograph for the required rivers. Ponte Vico's datum does not by itself define a boundary at the frozen AOI outlet, and Ponte Braldo's datum remains missing. No stage was converted to discharge, no missing datum became zero and the conditioned replay remains blocked.

conditionedReplayHydrographAudits.methodologyNote: Materialized after the conditioned-input protocol freeze from the official 12 December 2023 regional Commission report, recovered byte-for-byte from its 30 December 2023 Internet Archive capture because the current publisher URL returns not found. Page 57 states that the Commission used the 2022 ARPAE rating curve at Montone/Castrocaro; page 58 publishes Figure 63 as an hourly plotted discharge hydrograph; page 59 publishes the rounded rainfall and discharge volume balance. ARPAE DET-2024-723 subsequently documents that the available Castrocaro scale was calibrated on direct low-flow measurements only and commissioned a flood-branch calibration using at least two historical events, separate calibration and validation events, plus assessment of non-bijective h-Q or flood-loop behaviour. The same procurement requires measured-versus-modelled event hydrographs for Topkapi Montone-Rabbi and HEC-RAS Montone, with delivery requested by 2025-12-31, but does not itself publish the resulting numerical deliverables. The Commission report does not publish the rating-curve formula/table, machine-readable hourly discharge values, a numerical peak discharge or a Rabbi discharge hydrograph. No chart digitization, stage-to-discharge inference or missing-value substitution is performed, and the conditioned replay remains blocked.

conditionedReplayPhysicalAudits.methodologyNote: Materialized after the conditioned-input protocol freeze from the official March 2024 special-plan monograph and the official PAI hydraulic-relation directory. The monograph preserves local-gauge-zero peak stages and identifies where overtopping and breaches occurred, but it does not provide exact coordinates, activation times, crest/invert elevations, breach width evolution or hydrographs. The PAI relation documents a historical steady-flow HEC-RAS analysis, design discharges and roughness context, while the three downloaded public archives contain only DWG drawings. Historical design capacity or a statement that model files once existed is not an event-valid 2023 boundary or a usable channel model. No stage was converted to discharge, no narrative location was promoted to geometry and the replay remains blocked.

aoiRelation.transformation: proj4 EPSG:23032 ED50 UTM32 to EPSG:32632 with towgs84=-87,-98,-121,0,0,0,0

conditionedReplayTerrainAudits.methodologyNote: The official WCS DescribeCoverage declares a native 1 m EPSG:23032 grid and -3 as null. The bounded diagnostic request transforms the frozen EPSG:32632 AOI corners into an integer EPSG:23032 envelope and requests a 5 m nearest-neighbour representation only to audit source coverage before a full-resolution acquisition. The returned GeoTIFF omits a GDAL nodata tag, so -3 is interpreted only from the pinned DescribeCoverage rather than as elevation. The source is missing across 11.06% of the requested pixels and at material portions of known DBTR riverbed, embankment and permanent-water cell centres. A full 1 m download would preserve rather than repair those gaps, so it is not acquired at this gate. No -3 value becomes zero, terrain or an interpolated hydraulic surface.

This source tightens the acquisition gate; it does not satisfy it.
